A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveGPT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original scaling experiments, autonomous-vehicle planning results, WOMD motion-prediction results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports deployment latency and qualitative comparisons of larger models.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the encoder-decoder architecture, Verlet actions, teacher-forcing objective, autoregressive rollout, and K-Means subsampling. The additional probability-prediction head mentioned in v3 is a future-work suggestion, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: The internal dataset and WOMD planning/prediction coverage remain. Appendix D.1 and Figure 16 add a qualitative road-debris avoidance case, extending the explicitly demonstrated hazard scenarios. Newly named countries and day/night proportions describe the existing dataset rather than establish new training coverage.

E2.justification: The WOMD test comparison adds ControlMTR and MTR++ in v3 Table 5, corresponding to v2 Table 4. MTR, HDGT, HPTR, Wayformer Ensemble, and MotionLM Ensemble are retained; the ensemble methods receive revised labels.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the collision-rate description from trajectories overlapping with static agents to overlapping with traffic agents. This revises the reported metric definition, although the numerical entries remain unchanged and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.1 and Figure 16 compare collision avoidance by the 163M- and 94M-parameter models through two qualitative examples. Existing attention-head, encoder/decoder scaling, WOMD scaling, and failure-case analyses are retained after relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures. The existing scaling-fit reporting and figures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: HPTR soft mAP changes from 0.3904 in v2 Table 4 to 0.3968 in v3 Table 5, which also adds ControlMTR and MTR++ results. Existing DriveGPT numerical entries are retained. v3 additionally reports latency under 50 ms and qualitative collision-avoidance findings favoring the 163M model.

T1.justification: The chain-rule factorization, Verlet update, state/position definitions, and mathematical scaling relationships are retained. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and four main contributions retain the claims about large autoregressive driving models, empirical scaling laws, closed-loop deployment, and WOMD/pretraining benefits. The conclusion is reworded without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.3 extends the discussion of inaccurate trajectory probabilities and proposes a separate per-sample probability-prediction head as a possible remedy for poor soft mAP. The underlying probability-accumulation limitation and WOMD failure explanations already appear in v2.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the fixed, nonoverlapping 10-million-sample validation set, dataset geography and day/night balance, and Figure 1 baseline's relative scale. It also identifies the deployed model as an 8M model trained on the full dataset and reports operation on one onboard GPU. Existing training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including ControlMTR, MTR++, DrivingGPT, DrivingWorld, and ensemble-distillation scaling, and adds human intent to the related-work discussion. The PlanTF reference is removed although its Table 1 entry remains. The central research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose and author-information edits, expands dataset and deployment explanations, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Scaling configurations move into Section 4, while the appendix separates ablations and perplexity discussion; the main narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICML title/header formatting and reflows figures and tables. The configuration table moves from v2 Appendix B to v3 Section 4, the WOMD table gains rows and revised ensemble labeling, and Figure 16 is added. Earlier graphics are retained, including the failure cases renumbered Figure 17.

improvement.justification: v3 improves experimental transparency through validation-set and deployment details, broadens the WOMD comparison, and adds targeted evidence about larger-model collision avoidance. These are useful but limited gains because the central method and existing results remain stable. The unexplained collision-metric rewording leaves a small ambiguity that tempers the improvement.
